_comment: Bindings for Kit's OWN UI corpus (kit-ui.beh, beside this file). Every
accessible name below was read off the running app with a Playwright role
sweep — the same "nothing is invented" rule as every other corpus, and the
reason the corpus can be checked rather than believed.
Kit is TWO apps in its own registry: kit.beh (the CLI, "# kit:no-ui", derives
nothing and that is the finding) and kit-ui.beh (the browser surface, which is
what kit.beh's header predicted would change the number).
⚠️ EVERY NOUN IS PREFIXED Kit* AND NO LONGER NEEDS TO BE. The prefix dodged a
global namespace — an unprefixed page:Home here would have inherited snip-it's
"./" and emitted a test that runs against the wrong app with no unbound-noun
warning. A corpus now binds its own nouns, so that cannot happen. Renaming is
a corpus change and therefore James's (claude-code-bot#58).
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, honest refusals rather than gaps:
status:WriteNote — the "written, not committed" note has role=status but NO
accessible name, so it cannot be addressed by role+name. Its content is
the assertion worth making, and the notation has no way to ask for it.
the disabled-ness of button:KitDeny — `sees` proves a control EXISTS, not
that it is disabled. Boolean control state is unassertable in this grammar,
so it stays a `contract` line and is counted as one.
